messages.content: 尋找兩家電影院，位於聖地牙哥附近，提供下午5點的《天能》和晚上7點半的《007生死交戰》場次。

function.name: find_movie_showing
function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

message.reasoning:
The user wants two cinemas near San Diego offering showtimes at specified times for movies Tenet (the Chinese title 天能) and No Time To Die (007生死交戰). They want theaters located near San Diego.

We need to use the tool find_movie_showing with location=San Diego, CA presumably. Provide movie options as either Tenet or No Time To Die. But we have two separate queries? We can call twice: one for Tenet at time 5pm; second for No Time To Die at 7:30 pm. Or combine into single request? The function expects array of times but only one movie per call. So do two calls.

But they ask for two cinemas. That means each query should return multiple results maybe more than one cinema. We'll get list from API. Then pick first two unique locations? Actually they said "two cinemas". Could interpret as provide two distinct theater names that meet criteria. Might require filtering after retrieving data.

We'll call find_movie_showing twice:

1st call: location="San Diego, CA", movie="Tenet", time=["5:00 PM"] or just ["5:00"]. Use format likely "5:00 PM".

2nd call: same location, movie="No Time To Die", time=["7:30 PM"]

Then parse responses. If there are less than two theaters found overall across both queries, might not satisfy requirement. But assume enough.

Return answer listing two theaters with details.

Let's proceed.
